 Column: Miresse discusses minimum wage proposal, reminds voters of election dates 
 November 1, 2026 
 Hello neighbors,
 In 2009, the minimum wage was set at $7.25 per hour. In the 17 years since, consumer prices have risen by roughly 56%, while the state minimum wage has remained stagnant. Average costs for everyday necessities, such as food and fuel, continue to increase, creating significant financial strain for families across Wisconsin. In Portage County, a family of four with two working adults requires a household income of over $113,000 before taxes — or approximately $27 per hour per parent — to meet basic living expenses.
 To address this issue, my Democratic colleagues and I introduced legislation earlier this session to raise the state minimum wage to $15 per hour. This change would align Wisconsin with neighboring states, including Illinois ($15 per hour), Michigan ($13.73 per hour), and Minnesota ($11.41 per hour).
 The proposed legislation includes an annual increase of $1.25 per hour until the minimum wage reaches $20 per hour in 2030, after which it will be indexed to inflation. On Oct. 7, I hosted a Living Wage town hall with MASH President Peter Rickman to discuss why these adjustments are necessary for the economic well-being of workers across our state. I remain committed to advocating for fair wages for all Wisconsinites.
 Additionally, with the upcoming election approaching, please note the following key voting dates:
 Early Voting: Oct. 20-Nov. 1
 Election Day: Nov. 3
 Wisconsin permits same-day voter registration at polling places. Individuals registering on Election Day must present a valid photo ID and proof of residence. To check your voter registration status, locate your polling place, view a sample ballot, or review acceptable ID requirements, please visit myvote.wi.gov.
 As always, my office is here to help. If you have questions about state policy or need assistance with government services, please do not hesitate to reach out.
 Phone: (608) 237-9171
 Email: [email protected] 
 It’s an honor to serve you.
 — Rep. Vincent Miresse
Wisconsin State Assembly, District 71
